name: AD HOC Sync for Cassa in Cloud for WooCommerce
author: adhocsrl

sections.description:
AD HOC Sync for Cassa in Cloud for WooCommerce connects your WooCommerce store to Cassa in Cloud: the products, prices and stock levels you manage at the till reach your website on their own, so you never sell online what you have run out of in the shop.

Everything in this plugin works right away and without limits:

  • Import of products, prices and stock levels from Cassa in Cloud, including variations (size, color…).
  • Sale price taken from a Cassa in Cloud selling mode.
  • Automatic updates every 8 hours or every day, or whenever you start them yourself.
  • Four-step setup wizard and an import preview that shows what would change without modifying anything.
  • Health status, site check, activity log and WP-CLI commands (wp cassasync import).
  • Compatible with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).

Cassa Sync Premium (separate plugin)

Cassa Sync Premium is a separate plugin, available on the author’s website, that adds further features such as sending orders to Cassa in Cloud. It is not needed to use this plugin, which has no limits or locked features.

Trademarks and affiliation

AD HOC Sync for Cassa in Cloud for WooCommerce is developed by AD HOC SRL. It is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by WooCommerce or Automattic, nor by Cassa in Cloud or TeamSystem S.p.A. As in many other plugins, “for WooCommerce” in the name only describes the platform the plugin works with. WooCommerce and Cassa in Cloud are trademarks of their respective owners.

External services

This plugin connects to the Cassa in Cloud service (the point-of-sale software by TeamSystem S.p.A., formerly CassaNova) through its public API (https://api.cassanova.com). The service is required: without a Cassa in Cloud account the plugin has nothing to import.

  • What it is used for: to read the products, prices, stock levels, stores, selling modes and departments that you manage in Cassa in Cloud, and import them into WooCommerce.
  • When: when you start or schedule an import; when you save the API key in the settings or use “Reload stores, price lists and departments” (to read stores, selling modes and departments); once a day, to keep selling modes and departments up to date; in the setup wizard; and with “Test connection” and “Check the site” (which also calls the service’s health check).
  • What is sent: the API key you enter (to obtain an access token), your Cassa in Cloud store identifiers, and the requests that read the data above. This plugin does not send your customers’ data or orders to Cassa in Cloud.
  • Product images: during an import, the plugin downloads the product images whose addresses are returned by the service and saves them in your WordPress media library. Your server requests each image address; no data of yours is sent with the request.
  • Terms of service: https://www.teamsystem.com/terms-conditions/ (Cassa in Cloud conditions: https://tc.teamsystem.com/CassainCloud.pdf)
  • Privacy policy: https://www.teamsystem.com/privacy-policy/

Apart from the Cassa in Cloud API and the product images described above, this plugin does not contact any other server.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install and activate AD HOC Sync for Cassa in Cloud for WooCommerce.
  3. Open AD HOC Sync for Cassa in Cloud for WooCommerce in the menu and follow the setup wizard: Cassa in Cloud API key, store and price lists, import rules, preview and start.

The API key is created in Cassa in Cloud: Account settings › API. This plugin only reads data, so the “Read” permission is enough.
sections.faq:
Does AD HOC Sync for Cassa in Cloud for WooCommerce limit the number of products?

No. The import has no product limit.

Can I try it before importing?

Yes: the preview shows how many products would be created, updated or set to draft, without changing anything.

What happens to products that exist only on WooCommerce?

You choose in the settings: they are left as they are, set to draft or moved to the trash.

Does the plugin send emails?

No.
